name: Core Whodunnit
description: Structural and rhythm patterns measured directly from the text: uniform sentences and paragraphs, stacked connectives, repeated openers, and dense qualifiers or intensifiers.

rules.name: Uniform sentence rhythm
rules.description: Sentence lengths barely vary, so the prose reads at one monotonous pace.

remediation.guidance: Let some sentences be short and plain and others run longer, where the thought calls for it. Do not add or drop content to create variety.

rules.rationale: Very even sentence lengths across a sustained prose passage can signal mechanical cadence, but the statistic says nothing about authorship or quality on its own.
rules.falsePositiveNotes: Technical instructions and intentionally measured prose can be even. Needs at least 12 prose sentences and 180 words; treat the finding as a suggestion, not a target to game.

rules.name: No short or long sentences
rules.description: A long passage with no sentence under 8 words and none over 30.

remediation.guidance: Where a point lands, let it land in a short sentence; where an idea has parts, let it take a longer one.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: Only fires on 200+ words and 12+ sentences.

rules.name: Uniform paragraph blocks
rules.description: Paragraphs are nearly identical in length, which reads as assembled rather than written.

remediation.guidance: Observe the paragraph shape in context. A consistent format can serve a procedural or formal document.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: Lists, tables and templates are excluded. Needs 4+ prose paragraphs.

rules.name: Symmetrical paragraphs
rules.description: Every paragraph has exactly the same number of sentences.

remediation.guidance: Check whether a repeated structure serves the document before proposing any paragraph changes.

rules.name: Connective-heavy sentences
rules.description: A large share of sentences open with a stock connective (However, Moreover, Additionally, Therefore).

remediation.guidance: Check whether each transition states a real relationship. Formal signposting can be useful; frequency alone is not a reason to remove it.

rules.name: Stacked connectives
rules.description: The same connective opens several sentences, or additive connectives (Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally) are chained.

remediation.guidance: Keep at most one additive connective; drop the rest and let the sentences follow each other.

problematic: It works. Furthermore, it scales. Moreover, it is cheap.
preferred: It works, it scales, and it is cheap.

rules.name: Repeated sentence openings
rules.description: Consecutive sentences start with the same word, or one two-word opening recurs throughout.

remediation.guidance: Vary how sentences begin by leading with what matters in each one, not by swapping synonyms.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: Common openers (The, I, We, It, This) need a run of four; deliberate anaphora in stylised prose can trip this.

problematic: Honestly, it works. Honestly, it is fast. Honestly, it is cheap.
preferred: It works, it is fast, and it is cheap.

rules.name: Repeated paragraph openings
rules.description: Three or more consecutive paragraphs open with the same word.

remediation.guidance: Open each paragraph with its own point.

rules.name: Lists of three by default
rules.description: Several three-item lists in a short span, a rhythm that makes prose sound templated.

remediation.guidance: Check whether the three-item lists are complete and useful. Keep every real item, especially in procedures and technical inventories.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: One or two triads are ordinary; needs three or more and about one per 150 words.

rules.name: Dense intensifiers
rules.description: Many intensifiers (very, really, truly, incredibly) relative to length.

remediation.guidance: Cut intensifiers that add length but not meaning, or replace them with the specific fact that makes the thing notable.

rules.name: Dense hedging
rules.description: Qualifiers (may, might, perhaps, arguably, seems) are unusually dense across the text.

remediation.guidance: Check whether repeated qualifiers carry distinct uncertainty. Keep every hedge that limits a claim or belongs to the author's register.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: Writing about genuinely open questions hedges legitimately; the threshold is set high.

rules.name: Hedge cluster
rules.description: One paragraph carries four or more qualifiers.

remediation.guidance: Check each qualifier against the claim it limits. Repetition alone does not make a hedge expendable.
Most semicolons can become full stops, or commas with a conjunction.

rules.name: Mostly passive voice
rules.description: Nearly half the sentences look passive, which can hide who did what.

remediation.guidance: Where the actor is known and matters, name them.

rules.falsePositiveNotes: The passive detector is a pattern heuristic (be-verb + participle); scientific methods sections use passive on purpose.

rules.name: Wordy stock phrases
rules.description: Long stock phrases with a plain equivalent (in order to → to, due to the fact that → because).

problematic: We met in order to utilize the budget.
preferred: We met to use the budget.

rules.name: Leftover tool markup
rules.description: Citation or reference placeholders left behind by a chat tool (e.g. oaicite, contentReference, turn0search0).

remediation.guidance: Delete the placeholder and add a real citation if one is needed.

rules.rationale: These strings are not prose. The rule reports leftover markup; it says nothing about who wrote the text.

preferred: Revenue rose 4% last year (annual report, p. 12).
